findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3. `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, so on the real last page it is false and "next" stays enabled. Clicking "next" sets offset to `min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which equals `user_count`, and loads an empty page. The calculation should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset on the public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used without clamping. A client can pass `limit=1000000` and force the whole group, which may be tens of thousands of users, to be loaded and serialized in one request. Negative values are passed straight to SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, which makes PostgreSQL raise an error and the request returns a 500. The old code only applied pagination to automatic groups. This should cap the limit at a sane maximum and floor both values at 0.

findings.title: Breaking change to the response shape of /groups/:id/members, with no test
findings.body: The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. Any other consumer of the old shape, such as plugins or external API clients, will break. There is also no spec for `GroupsController#members` covering the new shape or the limit/offset behaviour. The only spec changes are in the admin controller spec.

findings.title: `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy
findings.body: The route now sets the controller model to the Group object instead of an array of members, so `{{#if model}}` is always true. The members table, including its header row, renders even before members load or when the group is empty. The condition should check `members`.

findings.title: Spec uses the wrong HTTP verb for remove_member
findings.body: The route for `remove_member` is `delete`, but the automatic-group test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It passes only because controller specs do not check the verb. The test therefore does not reflect the real route and would hide a verb constraint regression. It should use `xhr :delete`.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and ignores unknown user ids
findings.body: Membership is removed with `group.users.delete(user_id)` rather than `group.remove(user)`, which the old incremental-delete code used. This is inconsistent with `add_members`, which uses `group.add`, and it skips any logic in the model's remove path. There is also no handling for a user_id that does not belong to the group, so the controller reports success for a no-op.
